plain_english: Now the śrāddha-rule told in the venerable Ṣaḍardha is proclaimed.
sanskrit_cite: atha śrāddhavidhiḥ śrīmatṣaḍardhokto nigadyate

plain_english: In the Siddhātantra it is hinted, in the image-sacrifice exposition; and by funerary rite, for the well-purified and the impure, that is the rule.
sanskrit_cite: siddhātantre sūcito@sau mūrtiyāganirūpaṇe | antyeṣṭyā suviśuddhānāmaśuddhānāṃ ca tadvidhiḥ

plain_english: On the third day, on the fourth day, on the tenth, in the month, in the month, in the first year, year by year, at all times it is to be performed by his own as before.
sanskrit_cite: tryahe turye@hni daśame māsi māsyādyavatsare | varṣe varṣe sarvakālaṃ kāryastatsvaiḥ sa pūrvavat

plain_english: There as before he should worship the god, offer in fire likewise; then the food-offering itself, first taking it in hand's reach.
sanskrit_cite: tatra prāgvadyajeddevaṃ homayedanale tathā | tato naivedyameva prāggṛhītvā hastagocare

plain_english: The guru — the food-made, growing, potent-formed śakti — having meditated, by her the pervaded: that target let the wise one visualize.
sanskrit_cite: gururannamayīṃ śaktiṃ vṛṃhikāṃ vīryarūpiṇīm | dhyātvā tayā samāviṣṭaṃ taṃ sādhyaṃ cintayetsudhīḥ

plain_english: Then his fettered part, of enjoyable form — that he should offer; in the enjoyer, through identity-state: thus the disciple becomes Śiva.
sanskrit_cite: tato@sya yaḥ pāśavoṃ@śo bhogyarūpastamarpayet | bhoktaryekātmabhāvena śiṣya itthaṃ śivībhavet

plain_english: Enjoyableness and the other, body, frame — these are held fetter-natured; in śrāddha, in corpse-uplifting, in the final sacrifice: their Śiva-making.
sanskrit_cite: bhogyatānyā tanurdeha iti pāśātmakā matāḥ | śrāddhe mṛtoddhṛtāvantayāge teṣāṃ śivīkṛtiḥ

plain_english: Though fulfillment might come by a single rite, yet for the accomplishment of identity-state he should perform the whole rite.
sanskrit_cite: ekenaiva vidhānena yadyapi syātkṛtārthatā | tathāpi tanmayībhāvasiddhyai sarvaṃ vidhiṃ caret

plain_english: But for the enjoyment-seeker, in practice-abundance, in fruit-abundance as cause — therefore corpse-uplifting, śrāddha and the rest he should perform for him.
sanskrit_cite: bubhukṣostu kriyābhyāsabhūmānau phalabhūmani hetu | tato mṛtoddhāraśrāddhādyasmai samācaret

plain_english: But for him whose darkness is destroyed by the sun of tattva-knowledge, none of this — funerary rite, śrāddha rule and the rest — is ever of use.
sanskrit_cite: tattvajñānārkavidhvastadhvāntasya tu na ko@pyayam | antyeṣṭiśrāddhavidhyādirupayogī kadācana

plain_english: But for them — guru, his group, group-mates, fellow celibates, lineage-followers — the unity-day is a festival day.
sanskrit_cite: teṣāṃ tu guru tadvargavargyasabrahmacāriṇām | tatsantānajuṣāmaikyadinaṃ parvadinaṃ bhavet

plain_english: For when there is a surge of awakening, then — O festival day! — from fulfillment: birth-day and unity-day are therefore festivals through accomplished awakening.
sanskrit_cite: yadāhi bodhasyodrekastadā parvāha pūraṇāt | janmaikyadivasau tena parvaṇī bodhasiddhitaḥ

plain_english: And when the putraka may be of help to someone, then the mother's, father's, and śakti's channels running in the left-right interval —
sanskrit_cite: putrako@pi yadā kasmaicana syādupakārakaḥ | tadā mātuḥ pituḥ śaktervāmadakṣāntarālagāḥ

plain_english: he should make flow, to the deity he should offer the offered food; and in the venerable Bharuṇa tantra that was set forth by Śiva.
sanskrit_cite: nāḍīḥ pravāhayeddevāyārpayeta niveditam | śrīmadbharuṇatantre ca tacchivena nirūpitam

plain_english: And regard for their flowing-time is to be observed for the accomplishment of that form; then by spontaneity he should effect that accomplishment through the forthcoming rite.
sanskrit_cite: tadvāhakālāpekṣā ca kāryā tadrūpasiddhaye | svācchandyenātha tatsiddhiṃ vidhinā bhāvinā caret

plain_english: And in anyone's śrāddha, guru-deity-fire libation with wheel-sacrifice should be śrauta; but no fettered rite should there be.
sanskrit_cite: yasya kasyāpi vā śrāddhe gurudevāgnitarpaṇam | sacakreṣṭi bhavecchrauto natu syātpāśavo vidhiḥ

plain_english: And so it is said in the venerable Maukuṭa: established even in the Śiva-teaching, one who trusts in the Vedic rite is like a broken bell — nothing at all.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmaukuṭe tathā coktaṃ śivaśāstre sthito@pi yaḥ | pratyeti vaidike bhagnaghaṇṭāvanna sa kiṃcana

plain_english: And by the rite from stated god-worship to wheel-sacrifice, having reached Rudrahood, this creature fully enjoys divine pleasures.
sanskrit_cite: tathoktadevapūjādicakrayāgāntakarmaṇā | rudratvametyasau janturbhogāndivyānsamaśnute

plain_english: Now we speak clearly: for the venerable accomplishment, the channel-course — whichever channel one wishes to set flowing, that very one he should visualize.
sanskrit_cite: atha vacmaḥ sphuṭaṃ śrīmatsiddhaye nāḍicāraṇam | yā vāhayitumiṣyeta nāḍī tāmeva bhāvayet

plain_english: In visualization-identity that channel clearly flows; or, to set flowing whichever is desired — that limb, with that hand.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvanātanmayībhāve sā nāḍī vahati sphuṭam | yadvā vāhayituṃ yeṣṭā tadaṅgaṃ tena pāṇinā

plain_english: Pressing the belly, he should bend — it flows, the little channel, in a moment; thus even by means of śrāddha, the state of both enjoyment and liberation.
sanskrit_cite: āpīḍya kukṣiṃ namayetsā vahennāḍikā kṣaṇāt | evaṃ śrāddhamukhenāpi bhogamokṣobhayasthitim

plain_english: Let him effect it, thus — by compassionate Śiva said here and there; when śaktipāta has arisen for the creature, by whatever means the guide.
sanskrit_cite: kuryāditi śivenoktaṃ tatra tatra kṛpālunā | śaktipātodaye jantoryenopāyena daiśikaḥ

plain_english: He effects the uplifting, and that avails for his nirvāṇa; for the uplifter is the God of gods, he of inconceivable power.
sanskrit_cite: karotyuddharaṇaṃ tattannirvāṇāyāsya kalpate | uddhartā devadevo hi sa cācintyaprabhāvakaḥ

plain_english: To the means merely through the door of guru-initiation and the rest he should resort; told in the venerable so-called Mataṅga after the sage's question.
sanskrit_cite: upāyaṃ gurudīkṣādidvāramātreṇa saṃśrayet | uktaṃ śrīmanmataṅgākhye munipraśnādanantaram

plain_english: 'Liberation comes from discrimination of the tattvas — if from initiation, from yoga, how could it come from mere conduct?' — to this, a fitting answer.
sanskrit_cite: muktirvivekāttattvānāṃ dīkṣāto yogato yadi | caryāmātrātkathaṃ sā syādityataḥ samamuttaram

plain_english: Laughing, the Lord said: 'Whence your delusion about the Supreme Lord? For his all-gracing nature is well-established — look!'
sanskrit_cite: prahasyoce vibhuḥ kasmādbhrāntiste parameśituḥ | sarvānugrāhakatvaṃ hi saṃsiddhaṃ dṛśyatāṃ kila

plain_english: For one facing death, poison, disease, weapons and the rest are indeed the cause; whether small or great, that, in that manner meditated upon, is a cause of liberation.
sanskrit_cite: prāptamṛtyorviṣavyādhiśastrādi kila kāraṇam | alpaṃ vā bahu vā tadvadanudhyā muktikāraṇam

plain_english: For liberation's sake these outer marks are employed; knowing thus, there is no doubt — so it is to be done by the wise.
sanskrit_cite: muktyarthamupacaryante bāhyaliṅgānyamūni tu | iti jñātvā na sandeha itthaṃ kāryo vipaścitā

plain_english: 'How could liberation come by just this much?' — one should resort to supreme devotion. Told is the śrāddha-rule, crusher of delusion, poison, and dread.
sanskrit_cite: iyataiva kathaṃ muktiriti bhaktiṃ parāṃ śrayet | uktaḥ śrāddhavidhirbhrāntigarātaṅkavimardanaḥ
